Q: Initialising date with Date(milliseconds) constructor A:

The Answer by Jon Skeet correctly explains that your math fails because of integer overflow.

Another problem is that your code ignores the crucial issue of time zone.

The third challenge you faced was the awful bloody mess known as the legacy date-time classes. Never use Date, Calendar, Timestamp, SimpleDateFormat, etc.

Instead, let me show you the industry-leading modern java.time classes for all your date-time handling needs. These arrived built into Java 8 and later.

tl;dr

Use java.time classes in Java 8+.

LocalDate
.of( 1970 , Month.JANUARY , 26 )   // Represent a date-only value, without time-of-day, and without context of time zone or offset.
.atStartOfDay(                     // Determine the first moment of that date in that zone. May or may not be the time 00:00.
    ZoneId.of( "Asia/Kolkata" )    // The current time zone for India. 
)                                  // Returns a `ZonedDateTime`. This represents a moment as seen through the wall-clock/calendar of a particular time zone. 
.toInstant()                       // Returns a `Instant`. Effectively adjusted from time zone to UTC (an offset of zero hours-minutes-seconds since temporal meridian of UTC). 
.toEpochMilli()                    // Returns a `long` integer number, a count of milliseconds since the epoch reference of 1970-01-01T00:00Z.

Going the other direction.

Instant
.ofEpochMilli( millis )            // Returns a `Instant` object.
.atZone(
    ZoneId.of( "Asia/Kolkata" )
)                                  // Returns a `ZonedDateTime` object.
.toLocalDate()                     // Returns a `LocalDate` object, a date-only, stripping out the time-of-day and the time zone.

java.time

To represent a moment as seen “in UTC” (an offset of zero hours-minutes-seconds from the temporal meridian of UTC), use the java.time.Instant class.

Capture the current moment in UTC:

Instant now = Instant.now() ;  // Current moment as seen in UTC, with an offset of zero.

Apparently you want a count of milliseconds since the epoch reference of first moment of 1970 in UTC, 1970-01-01T00:00Z. Call toEpochMilli.

long millis = now.toEpochMilli() ;

The Instant class resolves to nanoseconds (9 digits of fractional second) versus the mere milliseconds of the legacy class java.util.Date. So beware of data-loss when converting to a count of milliseconds.

Going the other direction, getting an Instant object from a count of milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00Z:

Instant instant = Instant.ofEpochMilli( millis ) ;

You seem to also be interested in the first moment of a date. For that we must have a time zone. For any given moment, the time and the date vary around the globe by time zone. “Tomorrow” in Tokyo Japan is simultaneously “yesterday” in Toledo Ohio US.

ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of( "Pacific/Auckland" );
LocalDate today = LocalDate.now( zone ) ;  // Today’s date as seen in that time zone.

Let java.time determine the first moment of that day in that zone. Never assume the day starts at 00:00. Some dates in some zones start at other times, such as 01:00.

ZonedDateTime start = today.atStartOfDay( zone ) ;

Get your count of milliseconds by extracting a Instant from our ZonedDateTime, effectively adjusting from that time zone to UTC (offset of zero).

long millis = start.toInstant().toEpochMilli() ;

Going the other direction, from millis to to that date-and-time.

ZonedDateTime zdt = Instant.ofEpochMilli( millis ).atZone( zone ) ;

Q: Sample simple GTK 3.0 GUI code that compiled fine last week now has numerous header compile errors even on re-installation of the GTX 3.0 libraries A:

Technically, gtkmm is not a part of gtk but a separate library built on top of gtk. It has its own configuration. If using pkg-config, one should use something like pkg-config --cflags --libs gtkmm-3.0.

Q: Why is C#8's switch expression invalid in expression tree? A:

A number of newer C# syntax features are not supported in expression trees. In fact, expression trees does not support any of the newer C# syntax which have been introduced after expression trees were originally introduced back in C# 3.

Microsoft classifies System.Linq.Expressions as "archived" (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/27790), which means they do not accept new features because "the risk of code change likely exceeds the benefit". So it is unlikely new features will ever be added.

Since expression trees is an object model separate from the compiler (Roslyn) object model, new syntax will not automatically be supported just because the compiler supports it. Support have to specifically be added to the expression tree object model. And then of course any consumer of expression trees (like Linq-providers) would have to add support for the new node types.

Reading the discussions here https://github.com/dotnet/csharplang/issues/2545 it seems there is no fundamental technical reason preventing adding support for new syntax. It just comes down to the amount of work required compared to the benefit, and concerns about backwards compatibility with existing linq-providers.

Adding new node types at the framework-level is probably the smallest problem. The issue is that all third-party linq-providers would have to be updated to support the new node types. Perhaps worse, existing linq-provides will probably fail with obscure runtime errors when receiving unsupported nodes.

Q: Self Hosted Integration Runtime unable to access on prem SQL Server A:

The login failed. Login failed for user 'NT SERVICE\DIAHostService'.

This is not a firewall error this is an authentication error.

You have not granted that windows user account NT SERVICE\DIAHostService access to your database.

This issue is identical to this one, which has instructions on how to solve:

Login failed for user 'IIS APPPOOL\ASP.NET v4.0'

To select data from a table in SQL Server you need three things set up:

  1. Network connectivity (this is fine for you, otherwise you'd get a network error)
  2. The user account granted connect access to the server / db (this is what the error is complaining about - you need to do this)
  3. The user account granted sufficient access to select from the table (you also need to do this)
